senses.definition: A regulated diet that excludes or constrains certain types of food, especially for health reasons; also, a book or similar setting out such regulations.

quotes.text: In general, beets, carrots, and turnips are all of aphrodisiac value in erotic dietary.
quotes.reference: 1961, Harry E. Wedeck, Dictionary of Aphrodisiacs, New York: The Citadel Press, page 42:

senses.definition: A prescribed meal plan setting out how the inhabitants of an institution (such as a prison, hospital etc.) should be fed, and on what foods.

quotes.text: “Do I understand that he asked for more, after he had eaten the supper allotted by the dietary?” “He did, sir,” replied Bumble.
quotes.reference: 1837 February, Boz [pseudonym; Charles Dickens], “Treats of Oliver Twist’s Growth, Education, and Board”, in Oliver Twist; […], volume I, London: Richard Bentley, […], published 1838, →OCLC, page 30:

quotes.text: I cannot speak with any confidence of the pre-war dietary of asylum patients, which no doubt differs widely in different asylums.
quotes.reference: 1921, Montagu Lomax, The Experiences of an Asylum Doctor, London: Allen & Unwin, page 119:

senses.definition: Pertaining to a prescribed diet; (generally), relating to what a person or animal eats.
examples: If you have any dietary requirements, please inform the kitchen staff.
